text:
anya: Heads-up: legal asked how we can prove "who changed what" without forcing full object snapshots into every export. They're getting lots of NDJSON exports and are overwhelmed with size. Thoughts?

sam: We should default to micro-diffs (path + old + new) and include a compact audit envelope (actor_id, ts, resource, change_hash). Full snapshots only when requested.

liam: Agree. Operationally we can offer 3 levels: none (diffs only), attach-on-demand (context_url), and embed (full snapshot inline). Attach-on-demand maps better to presigned URLs or a proxy fetch.

nora: From product, inline diffs are fine for daily use. But legal wants an easy "package" for e-discovery that includes snapshots + access logs. We'll need a UI flow for that and a checkbox that warns about size.

matt: Implementation detail: prefer a proxy-backed evidence_view endpoint instead of presigned S3 links. Proxy gives us centralized access logging and permission checks. We can still store encrypted blobs in S3.

anya: How do we keep export sizes reasonable while preserving verifiability? Could we store encrypted snapshot blobs and include a compact change_hash in the NDJSON that cryptographically links to the blob?

sam: Yes. NDJSON record example (single-line concept): {type: "change", id: "evt-xxx", ts: 1670000000, actor_id: "u123", resource: "policy/321", diff: [{path: ["rules",1], old: false, new: true}], change_hash: "sha256:...", snapshot_ref: "s3://..."} But the text blob is not in the stream. snapshot_ref becomes a proxy key.

liam: Quotas: introduce export_snapshot_bytes as a separate metric/quota. Also count snapshot downloads separately so customers know retrieval cost. UI should show estimated snapshot MB before confirm.

nora: UX: show "diffs included: yes" and a line "snapshots included: N (X MB)" with an info tooltip explaining retention and access control. For legal package we can auto-select snapshots for privileged events.

matt: Telemetry: emit export.created {has_snapshots, snapshot_bytes_estimate, reason_mode, actor_resolution} and export.snapshot_downloaded {actor_id, bytes}. This helps us decide defaults and potential billing.

anya: About reasons/justification text: sometimes the human intent is buried in a freeform justification. Legal sometimes needs that verbatim. Can we offer reason_mode: plaintext, redacted, hashed? hashed = sha256(reason) so you can verify but not read.

sam: Sounds good. hashed reasons acceptable for chain-of-custody. Provide an emergency retrieval flow (strict approvals + audit trail) for plaintext when required.

security-bot: Reminder: storing plaintext justifications requires stricter retention and encryption keys + KMS rotations. Proxy access must also require mfa for legal staff.

liam: On the proxy vs presigned debate: presigned URLs are cheaper but lose central auditing and revocation. Proxy is heavier but gives us a single place to enforce ACLs and capture who accessed what and when. I'm leaning proxy.

matt: If we proxy, make the endpoint stateless and cache short-lived tokens to avoid long-running sessions. Also add per-download metrics and throttle downloads to limit abuse.

anya: API proposal for creating exports: POST /exports with body flags: include_diffs (bool), snapshot_mode (none|minimal|all), reason_mode (plaintext|redacted|hash), actor_resolution (simple|resolved), proxy_snapshots (bool). Defaults: include_diffs=true, snapshot_mode=minimal, reason_mode=hash, actor_resolution=simple, proxy_snapshots=true.

sam: Default makes sense. minimal = include snapshots for events that are privileged or flagged by retention rules, not everything.

nora: Console will surface a "Legal package" preset that sets snapshot_mode=all and shows a pre-flight size estimate. It will also surface a link to start the strict approval flow for plaintext reasons.

matt: We'll need a small A/B to validate defaults. Track avg snapshot_bytes per export and download_rate. Set a soft cap that prompts customers when snapshot estimate exceeds threshold.

devops-bot: export-job-2720001111 queued by @anya (job-id ex-20260321-11b).

anya: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with NDJSON schema, snapshot storage plan (encrypted S3 + proxy), quota changes, and UI wireframes. Will tag @security and @legal for review.

devops-bot: export-job-2720001111 status: done (size: 4.1MB, snapshots: 0.9MB, records: 230).

matt: :thumbsup: thanks all.

anya: I'll ping when RFC is up.
